sections.h2: Which Thurston County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work, and all three are in the Atrium building at 3000 Pacific Ave SE in Olympia. The Treasurer bills and collects, the Assessor values property and runs exemptions, and the Board of Equalization hears value appeals.

  • Treasurer: 360-786-5550, trsr@co.thurston.wa.us, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday.
  • Assessor: 360-867-2200 or asrinfo@co.thurston.wa.us.
  • Board of Equalization: 360-786-5135. Outside the appeal season it serves people by appointment only.

The county announced that 2026 tax notices went out on February 9, 2026, and that the total assessed for all taxing districts was $652,290,192.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Thurston County?
sections.html:
Thurston County sits at the south end of Puget Sound along the I-5 corridor, with Olympia, the state capital, as county seat. Wikipedia's county entry lists Lacey, Tumwater, Yelm and Bucoda among the other incorporated places and notes that Lacey, with an estimated population above 60,000, has passed Olympia as the largest city. More than 145,000 people live in unincorporated areas, mostly between Olympia and Lacey.

The same entry says state government became the county's largest employment sector in the 1950s, which helps explain a housing market tied to Olympia area jobs. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table gives the current picture:

  • Population: 304,261 in July 2025, on 722.5 square miles of land.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 67.7 percent.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $480,300.
  • Median household income: $96,563.
  • Median gross rent: $1,736.

sections.h2: When are Thurston County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first half is late if unpaid after April 30, and the second half is late if unpaid after October 31. The Treasurer's FAQ page adds that a due date landing on a Saturday or Sunday moves to the following Monday. October 31, 2026 fell on a Saturday, so under that rule the second-half deadline became Monday, November 2, 2026, which has passed.

Payment routeCost or rule
Online electronic checkNo transaction fee
Online debit card1 percent or $2.00 minimum
Online credit card2.3 percent or $2.00 minimum
MailCounts if postmarked or received by the due date; a postage meter date does not count
In person or drop boxAtrium building, 3000 Pacific Ave SE

Sources: Thurston County Treasurer FAQ and the 2026 notice press release. Half payments are valid for the current year amount only until October 30, and real property taxes paid after that date must cover the whole year's balance. The county says the law allows no hardship extensions.

sections.h2: What happens when Thurston County taxes are late?
sections.html:
Interest runs on the whole year's tax from the date of delinquency, and real property can be sold for taxes once it is three full years behind. State law sets residential interest at 9 percent a year for properties with four or fewer units, with penalties of 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1 applying to other property types, as spelled out in RCW 84.56.020. The county FAQ describes the June and December penalties more generally, so call 360-786-5550 for the exact amount on your parcel.

  • A late payment has to include the late fees, or the Treasurer returns it.
  • Foreclosure on real property starts in June of each year and ends with a sale in the second week of January.
  • The Treasurer can set up a signed payment plan for delinquent prior years. For current year tax, the full amount due is required.
  • The county does not report delinquent tax to credit agencies, but the owner's name appears in a legal notice in a local newspaper.
  • If the sale brings in more than the tax and costs, the surplus goes to the owner.

The FAQ also points out that special assessments on the bill, such as stormwater, state forest fire protection, noxious weed control, conservation district, drainage district, lake management and septic program charges, are enforceable liens. The Treasurer will not accept tax alone without them.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Thurston County assessment?
sections.html:
You file a signed petition with the Board of Equalization by July 1 or 60 days after the Assessor mails the value notice, whichever is later. For the 2026 assessment year the Assessor mailed notices on September 16, 2026, and the board's 2026 appeals page set the deadline at 5 p.m. on Monday, November 16, 2026. If you are reading this after that date, the 2026 window has closed, and the late-filing rules below apply.

  • Use the county petition form with a handwritten signature, plus a copy of the front page of the value notice.
  • No email, fax or online filing is accepted for 2026. Mail, courier or hand delivery are the routes, and a mailed petition must be postmarked by the deadline.
  • File a separate petition for each parcel.
  • The board looks at market value only. It cannot consider the amount of tax, other properties' assessments, the percentage increase or personal hardship.

The county says hearings can take 12 to 18 months to be scheduled, and the Assessor's value is presumed correct, so the owner must bring clear, cogent and convincing evidence such as comparable sales, repair bids and photos. Late filing exceptions are limited and must be requested by April 30 of the following year. A decision can be appealed to the State Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days.

sections.h2: What property tax relief does Thurston County offer?
sections.html:
The senior and disability exemption is the largest program, and the Assessor runs it. Under the county's relief programs page, you qualify if you are 61 or older, or disabled and unable to work, or a disabled veteran rated 80 percent or higher (40 percent beginning in 2027). You also have to own and live in the home and have combined disposable income of $59,000 or less, rising to $83,000 beginning in 2027.

The Treasurer's FAQ says qualifying owners are exempt from voted taxes, which average about 40 percent of a Thurston County bill, and the program freezes the taxable value of the home. You still owe whatever is billed on the due date while an application is pending, and a refund follows if the Assessor approves it later.

Other programs worth asking about:

  • Senior and limited-income deferral, where the state pays the second half and places a lien. The limited-income version has a $57,000 income cap and requires five years of ownership.
  • Destroyed property relief, claimed within three years of the damage.
  • A three-year residential remodeling exemption, which must be filed before the work is done.
  • Current use classification for farm, timber and open space land.

sections.h2: How does property tax work at a Thurston County closing?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's FAQ says taxes follow the property rather than the person, and that you and the buyer decide in the closing how the year is split. Washington's default under RCW 84.60.020 prorates by the portion of the calendar year before and after the sale date, with the lien attaching on January 1.

Thurston County sends statements only once a year, in February, to the owner on record as of December 31. After a sale the new owner may not receive a bill, so tell the escrow officer which half remains open and let the title company confirm with the Treasurer. Name changes on the tax roll come through the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit filed with the county.

faqs.q: What is the Thurston County property tax deadline for 2026 second half?
faqs.a: October 31, 2026 fell on a Saturday, so the due date moved to Monday, November 2 under the county's weekend rule. That date has passed, so call the Treasurer at 360-786-5550 for your current balance and any late charges.

faqs.q: Can I get an extension on Thurston County property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer states that the law allows no extensions for hardship. A payment plan is available for delinquent prior years, and the senior and disability exemption or deferral may reduce or postpone tax if you qualify.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Thurston County assessed value?
faqs.a: Each year, by July 1 or 60 days from the notice mailing date. The 2026 notices went out September 16, and the board's deadline was 5 p.m. on November 16, 2026. File every year you disagree, because each petition stands alone.

faqs.q: How long before Thurston County forecloses on unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Real property becomes subject to sale when taxes are three full years delinquent. Foreclosure begins in June and the sale is held in the second week of January. Personal property and mobile homes can be collected as soon as they are late.

faqs.q: Who pays Thurston County property tax when a house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: Unless the contract says otherwise, the seller covers the part of the year before the sale date and the buyer covers the rest. The escrow officer settles the open half with the Treasurer, who sends statements once a year in February.
